items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1976-02-13
items.q: Some of the musicians I played with there was Chink Morton's son, Chink Morton Jr.

ctx.x: And then you went and played in the French Quarter for a while, I guess.

I went to work at a cabaret. It was called the Cabarets in those days. It was called the Valencia Cabaret. It was where the Royal Sinesta Hotel is today, on Bourbon Street. And I worked with various little groups, three-piece groups there, from time to time. Some of the musicians I played with there was Chink Morton's son, Chink Morton Jr. Eddie Miller played there with me for a while. Who's now playing with Pete Fountain. Yes. And Eddie played alto sax in those days. He wasn't playing tenor. And Al Hesman, banjo…

items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1960-07-14
items.q: And Chink Martin's son, Chink Junior, played banjo.

ctx.x: And what other bands did Gillen play with that you know of?

I don't know of any other bands that he played with, Dick. The only time that I had ever played with Bill was at the Fern Dance Hall. After I left the Fern Dance Hall, I'd like to mention that I went to my first nightclub job, or cabaret they called it in the old days, was the Valencia on Bourbon Street. That was about 1927, I think. And I played with a little outfit there. I believe it was Hilton Lamar's brother, Jimmy Lamar, played alto sax. And Chink Martin's son, Chink Junior, played banjo. Buck Rogers played…
I wonder where he got his style. I can't imagine.
